instructions:
## Research objective

Your goal is to design reasoning and prompt engineering techniques to maximize accuracy for learning score functions from partially observed data via marginal importance-weighted and variational score matching, with applications to parameter estimation and graphical model recovery under MCAR/MNAR missingness.

## Plan Formulation

- Reproduce and extend the paper’s two approaches: (1) marginal Importance-Weighted (IW) score matching and (2) marginal Variational (Gradient-First) score matching, both for MCAR missingness; optionally add MNAR per Appendix A.1.4.
- Implement four score matching variants: classical, truncated (with boundary weights g), sliced (random projections), and denoising; prioritize classical and truncated for core results, add sliced/denoising as ablations.
- Model classes to cover: Gaussian (mean/precision), an unnormalizable ICA-like model qθ(x) ∝ exp(Σ θ_i,j x_i^2 x_j^2), and Gaussian Graphical Models (GGMs) with L1 regularization for edge recovery.
- Primary comparisons: Marg-IW (ours), Marg-Var (ours), EM-like method (Uehara et al., 2020), and Zeroed Score Matching baseline (naive marginalization).
- Design synthetic regimes where methods differ: low-dim/small-n (favor IW), high-dim/complex structure (favor Variational).
- Define clear evaluation metrics per task: Fisher divergence and parameter error for estimation; ROC/AUC vs ground truth edges for graphical models.
- Hyperparameter grid to explore: IW sample count r (e.g., 5, 10, 50), variational inner steps L per θ update (e.g., 1, 5, 10), learning rates, missingness probabilities, truncation settings, and projection counts for sliced SM.
- Ensure identifiability assumptions (Assumption 4.2e) hold for chosen parameterizations; use well-specified synthetic ground truths.
- Plan for numerical stability and variance control: log-sum-exp for IW, clipping/normalizing weights, reparameterization for variational sampling, gradient norm monitoring.
- Target reproducibility: fix seeds, log software/hardware, pin package versions, and export exact configs.

## Data Preparation

- Synthetic Gaussian (10-D): sample Σ with random eigenvectors and eigenvalues in [0.5, 1.5]; set strong dependency between dims 1 and 10 (e.g., X10 = 0.5 X1 + 0.5 Z, Var(Z)=Var(X1)); fix µ = 0.5·1.
- Truncation for Gaussian: truncate along first 3 coordinates above their 10% quantiles; for truncated SM define boundary-aware weights g that vanish at ∂X (e.g., distance-to-boundary or smooth proxy).
- Synthetic ICA-like density: qθ(x) ∝ exp(Σ_i,j θ_i,j x_i^2 x_j^2); sample data from a fixed θ* via rejection or annealed Langevin on the unnormalized density; create dimensional settings {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}.
- Graph structures for GGM:
-   - Star graph: 1 high-degree hub with edges to others; sample Gaussian with precision P consistent with graph.
-   - Dense/unstructured: include each edge independently with p=0.5.
-   - Vary number of star centers while keeping overall edge density fixed.
- Real datasets:
-   - S&P 100: daily closing prices (2013–2018), compute log-returns, standardize per feature; ground-truth adjacency from fully observed score matching.
-   - Yeast gene expression (GSE1990): select 106 genes present in ≥95% samples, z-score each gene; ground-truth adjacency from fully observed score matching.
- Missingness generation: MCAR masks M ∈ {0,1}^d per-sample; per-coordinate missing probability p ∈ {0.2,…,0.9}; store Λ (observed index set) alongside masked sample X_Λ.
- Optional MNAR: define φ_λ(X)=P(E_λ|X) known; assemble training pairs (X_Λ, λ) and compute missing-score integrands with φ_λ as in Appendix A.1.4.
- For sliced SM: predefine number of projections K and sample V_λ ∈ R^{|λ|} with E[V_λ V_λ^T] ≻ 0 (e.g., V_λ ~ N(0,I)); store seeds.
- For denoising SM: define noise schedules m(t), σ(t) with increasing σ; ensure per-coordinate independence for constructing marginal transition kernels p_λ(x_λ(t)|x_λ(0)).
- Data splits: create multiple random seeds; batch sizes of 100 recommended; for Gaussian/ICA generate n in {200, 400, …, 1000}; ensure logs of masks and Λ sets are persisted.

## Running Experiments

- Core libraries: implement in PyTorch or JAX with auto-diff; enable double precision for stability in precision estimation; use vectorized operations over batch and IW samples.
- Common utilities:
-   - Mask handling: given X and mask M, produce Λ and X_Λ; zero-filled variant X^0_λ for baselines.
-   - qθ and sθ: expose log qθ(x) and sθ(x)=∇_x log qθ(x) for all models (Gaussian: param via µ and Cholesky of precision; ICA-like: polynomial score).
-   - Truncation weights g: implement differentiable g(x) that smoothly vanishes at ∂X; cache ∇g where needed.
- Marginal IW score estimate:
-   - Choose p′(x_{-λ}) that is samplable/evaluable (e.g., isotropic Gaussian with variance 16 as in paper);
-   - For each sample (X_Λ, λ), draw r IID X′_{-λ} ~ p′; compute
-     u_k = log qθ(X_Λ, X′_{-λ}^{(k)}) - log p′(X′_{-λ}^{(k)});
-     use log-sum-exp to compute log mean exp(u_k);
-     ŝ_{λ,r;θ}(X_Λ) = ∇_{x_λ} log mean_k exp(u_k) via auto-diff.
-   - Construct LM/TM empirical objective by replacing s_λ;θ with ŝ_{λ,r;θ} in classical or truncated forms;
-   - Optimize θ with Adam (lr≈1e-2) for T iterations; typical r=10 (also test r∈{5,10,50}); monitor stability; clip extremely large IW weights.
- Gradient-First (Variational) approach:
-   - Conditional variational model p′_ϕ(x_{-λ}|x_λ): Gaussian with mean µ_ϕ(x^0_λ)_{-λ} (2-layer MLP width 200) and fixed σ_ϕ;
-   - Train ϕ to match pθ(x_{-λ}|x_λ) by minimizing JF(ϕ,θ) or JKL(ϕ,θ) from Proposition 4.12 using samples (X_Λ, X′_{-Λ}) with reparameterization;
-   - Per θ step:
-     1) For l in 1..L (e.g., L=10): sample X′_{-Λ} ~ p′_ϕ(.|X_Λ) for all batch points; update ϕ by SGD/Adam on ˆJF/ˆJKL;
-     2) Resample r variational draws per data point; compute Monte Carlo estimates of E′[·] and Cov′[·] needed by Corollary 4.9 (and 4.11 if truncated);
-     3) Build pseudo-loss with detached θ′ (Appendix A.5) or compute gradient d∇_θ LM/TM(θ) directly; update θ.
-   - Use reparameterization trick for sampling; ensure covariances are unbiased; optionally control variance with antithetics or control variates.
- Baselines:
-   - EM-like (Uehara et al., 2020): implement self-normalized importance weighting nested estimates as in the reference; match settings (r, p′) to ours.
-   - Zeroed Score Matching: zero-impute missing entries X^0_λ and compute loss only over observed output coordinates; for Gaussian, note mismatch P_{λ,λ} vs Schur complement.
- GGM training with L1:
-   - Optimize θ=(µ,P) under LM/TM plus L1 penalty on off-diagonal P entries via proximal gradient (soft-thresholding off-diagonals each step);
-   - Learning rate ν≈1e-2; run 200 iters at a large γ, then decrease γ every 10 iters over a log-spaced grid (e.g., γ ∈ [10^{-1.7},10^{-4}] synthetic; [10^{1},10^{-4}] real);
-   - After each γ block, threshold small |P_{ij}| to form adjacency; compute TPR/FPR vs ground truth; build ROC and AUC.
- Experiment matrix:
-   - Gaussian estimation: n ∈ {200,…,1000}, MCAR p=0.2, r=10, 200–1000 optimization steps; evaluate Fisher divergence, mean L2 error, precision Frobenius error.
-   - ICA-like: n=1000, missing p=0.5, d∈{10,20,30,40,50}; evaluate parameter error (L2 of θ).
-   - Star/dense GGMs: missing p∈{0.2,…,0.9}, truncated via random hyperplane (retain ~80%); measure AUC; repeat over seeds to get CIs.
-   - Vary number of star centers at fixed edge density; measure impact on AUC and on naive marginalization performance.
-   - Real S&P100 and Yeast: MCAR with multiple p; ground truth adjacency from fully observed SM at fixed densities; per-method AUC averaged across densities.
- Engineering and checks:
-   - Use gradient clipping; watch for exploding IW weights; add small eps in denominators; sanity-check sθ on fully observed subsets.
-   - Verify Assumptions for truncated SM (regularity, boundary conditions) and classical SM (Hyvärinen conditions).
-   - Time/space complexity: Marg-IW O(nr) per epoch; Marg-Var adds inner L steps; log compute time per run.
-   - Log seeds, masks, Λ distributions, hyperparameters, and exact random streams for reproducibility.

## Results Interpretation

- Report Fisher divergence trends vs sample size n for truncated Gaussian; expect Marg-IW and EM best at small/low-d settings, Marg-Var approaching asymptotically; Zeroed does not converge.
- For ICA-like model, expect Marg-Var to dominate as d increases; analyze sensitivity to missingness and n; compare θ error across methods.
- For GGMs:
-   - Star graphs: Marg-Var should yield highest AUC across missingness; quantify gaps and CI; show representative ROC curves.
-   - Dense/unstructured: smaller gap; explain why naive marginalization can be competitive when structure is less pronounced.
-   - Increasing star centers: diminishing advantage of Marg-Var; link to marginal precision structure and naive marginalization behavior.
- Real datasets: Marg-Var should outperform others consistently across missingness levels; discuss implications for practical high-d tabular data.
- Ablations:
-   - IW r-sweep: effect on bias/variance and runtime; note O(nr) scaling and r≈n for √n rates (theory) vs practical r≈10.
-   - Variational inner steps L and σ_ϕ: convergence speed and gradient variance; JF vs JKL behavior when qθ normalization unknown.
-   - Truncated vs classical: show necessity of g near boundaries and impact on stability/accuracy.
-   - Optional sliced/denoising variants: projection count K and noise schedule sensitivity.
- Diagnostics:
-   - Compare E′ and Cov′ estimates across methods; verify equivalence trends between IW gradient and Variational gradient (Appendix A.3) when p′ independent of x_λ.
-   - Inspect precision matrices: Schur complement vs naive P_{λ,λ}; visualize where Zeroed fails.
- Theoretical caveats: marginal Fisher vs full Fisher gap (Remark 4.7); discuss identifiability assumptions and when they may fail.

## Report Writing

- Document experimental setup with precise configs: model definitions, objectives used (classical/truncated), missingness distributions, truncation schemes, and all hyperparameters (r, L, learning rates, γ schedule).
- Present results:
-   - Estimation: curves of Fisher divergence vs n; tables for mean/precision errors; ICA θ errors vs d and missingness.
-   - GGM: ROC curves and AUC with 95% confidence intervals; edge density vs γ; example adjacency visualizations.
-   - Real data: AUC across missingness and ground-truth densities; threshold selection procedure and smoothing criterion.
- Include ablation studies and runtime/memory profiles; discuss scalability and when to prefer IW vs Variational.
- Provide implementation notes:
-   - Numerical stability tactics (log-sum-exp, clipping, detach tricks for pseudo-loss), auto-diff frameworks, reparameterization for variational sampling.
-   - Assumptions and regularity conditions checked; boundary handling for truncated SM.
- Reproducibility: list seeds, OS/GPU/CPU, package versions; release code with config files and scripts for each figure; archive masks and Λ patterns.
- Discussion and future work: bridging marginal-to-full Fisher guarantees, MNAR generalization with φ_λ learning, diffusion-based extensions via denoising SM, and deeper analysis of IW–Variational equivalences.
- Ethical and impact statement: note applicability to real-world missing tabular data; limitations due to missingness mechanisms and modeling assumptions.
